notes: Six province-level metrics from four primary Stats SA releases. Periods and denominators differ; do not combine them into an undated composite score.
No municipality-level estimates or interpolated missing values have been created.
Values are published or reproducibly derived; null is reserved for unavailable observations.
No claim of live or continuously updated data.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Official unemployment rate
metrics.definition: Unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force, ages 15–64, using the official unemployment definition.
metrics.denominator: Employed plus officially unemployed persons aged 15–64 (labour force).
caveats: Official unemployment is distinct from combined unemployment and potential labour force (LU3).
Survey sampling uncertainty is not displayed in this snapshot; avoid interpreting small differences as statistically significant.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Employment absorption rate
metrics.definition: Employed persons as a percentage of the working-age population, ages 15–64.
metrics.denominator: All persons aged 15–64, including those outside the labour force.
caveats: This is an employment-to-working-age-population rate, not the complement of the unemployment rate.
Survey sampling uncertainty is not displayed in this snapshot.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Real provincial GDP growth
metrics.definition: Annual percentage change in provincial GDP measured at constant 2022 prices.
metrics.denominator: Previous calendar year provincial GDP in the same constant-2022-price release vintage.
metrics.method: Published one-decimal percentage changes from Table 2; not recalculated from rounded rand-million levels.
caveats: Growth is not the size, share or per-capita income of a provincial economy.
The October 2026 rebased release revises prior years; do not mix its growth estimates with earlier vintages.
All values reflect 2025; the release month and retrieval date are separate from the measurement period.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Adults with no schooling
metrics.definition: Share of persons aged 20 and older whose highest educational attainment category was no schooling.
metrics.denominator: All persons aged 20 and older in Table 4.6, including the Other attainment category.
metrics.method: Calculated as 100 × published category count / published provincial total aged 20+; rounded to one decimal for display. Raw category and denominator counts retained.
caveats: This denominator is ages 20+, not ages 25+ or all residents.
Census attainment categories measure highest attainment, not current enrolment or education quality.
Published rounded category counts can differ by a few persons when summed; use the published total denominator without forcing reconciliation.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Adults with post-school education
metrics.definition: Share of persons aged 20 and older whose highest educational attainment category was post-school.
metrics.denominator: All persons aged 20 and older in Table 4.6, including the Other attainment category.
metrics.method: Calculated as 100 × published category count / published provincial total aged 20+; rounded to one decimal for display. Raw category and denominator counts retained.
caveats: This denominator is ages 20+, not ages 25+ or all residents.
Census attainment categories measure highest attainment, not current enrolment or education quality.
Published rounded category counts can differ by a few persons when summed; use the published total denominator without forcing reconciliation.

metrics.aggregation: Do not sum or average provincial rates; the national value is separately sourced.
metrics.name: Medical aid coverage
metrics.definition: Percentage of individuals who are members of a medical aid scheme, as published by Stats SA.
metrics.denominator: Individuals represented by the General Household Survey; published medical-aid membership rates retained rather than reconstructed from rounded counts.
metrics.method: Published Figure 5.3 one-decimal rates, corroborated by selected development indicators Table 2.4; not computed from rounded counts.
caveats: Financial insurance coverage is an access proxy; it does not measure public healthcare access, service availability, quality, facility capacity or health outcomes.
People without medical aid can still receive care through public services.
Unknown or unspecified coverage statuses are handled as in the published Stats SA estimates; no observations were imputed.
Survey sampling uncertainty is not displayed; do not interpret small provincial differences as statistically significant.
